claims.claim_text: ELISA analysis of serum from 56 healthy volunteers after primary vaccination (day 0) and secondary vaccination (day 21) showed anti-spike IgG binding antibody responses were induced after the first dose and boosted significantly after the second dose.

source.quote: Primary vaccination induced binding antibody and neutralizing antibody responses in all but three individuals; these responses were boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination ( Fig. 1a , b , Extended Data Fig. 1b – d ).

claims.claim_text: Bulk RNAseq analysis of whole blood from 31 participants showed secondary vaccination (day 21) generated a greater transcriptional response than primary vaccination (day 0), with nearly a fourfold increase in differentially expressed genes at day 22 versus day 1 and induction of antiviral, interferon, dendritic cell activation, Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte and neutrophil modules after the boost.

source.quote: Secondary vaccination generated a greater transcriptional response (as has previously been seen in a recent study of adjuvanted hepatitis B vaccine 17 ), with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 as compared to day 1 ( Fig. 3a ); this is consistent with the increased markers of innate immunity detected by both CyTOF and Olink ( Fig. 2 ).

sources.quote: Secondary vaccination generated a greater transcriptional response (as has previously been seen in a recent study of adjuvanted hepatitis B vaccine 17 ), with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 as compared to day 1 ( Fig. 3a ); this is consistent with the increased markers of innate immunity detected by both CyTOF and Olink ( Fig. 2 ).

Gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that both doses of BNT162b2 stimulated antiviral and interferon response modules 18 ( Fig. 3b ). However, the booster immunization led to a broader innate response. In addition to the induction of antiviral pathways, secondary vaccination led to increases in signatures of dendritic cell activation and the upregulation of Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte and neutrophil modules on days 22 and 23 ( Fig. 3b , Extended Data Fig. 8c , d ).
Next, we performed bulk mRNA sequencing of whole blood from 31 participants.

claims.claim_text: CITEseq assay analysis of 45 PBMC samples from 6 individuals showed that one day after secondary vaccination (day 22), cluster C8 emerged and increased about 100-fold versus one day after primary vaccination (day 1), with expression of interferon-stimulated genes WARS, GBP1, IFI30 and IFITM3 and reduced AP-1 transcription factors FOS and JUN.

source.quote: We performed cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing (CITE-seq) of 45 peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples from 6 individuals ( Extended Data Fig. 1a ) to disentangle these two effects and to examine transcriptional changes at the single-cell level.

sources.quote: We performed cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing (CITE-seq) of 45 peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples from 6 individuals ( Extended Data Fig. 1a ) to disentangle these two effects and to examine transcriptional changes at the single-cell level.

Notably, cluster C8 (which expressed CD14 , VCAN , CD1C , FCGR1A and CD274 mRNA or protein) emerged on day 22, one day after secondary vaccination ( Fig. 4b ). These cells uniquely expressed interferon-stimulated genes, including WARS (also known as WARS1 ), GBP1 , IFI30 and IFITM3 ( Extended Data Fig. 9d ), and constituted about 0.01% of the Lin − HLA-DR + population on day 1 after primary vaccination but increased almost 100-fold to about 1% one day after secondary vaccination ( Fig. 4c ).
In addition to expressing higher interferon-stimulated genes as compared to their parent clusters, they had a reduced expression of the AP-1 transcription factors FOS and JUN ( Fig. 4f ).

comparison.finding: Cluster C8 emerged at day 22 and increased about 100-fold versus day 1, with expression of interferon-stimulated genes WARS, GBP1, IFI30 and IFITM3 and reduced AP-1 transcription factors FOS and JUN.

claims.claim_text: CyTOF analysis of whole blood from 27 individuals showed inflammatory intermediate monocytes (CD14+ CD16+ monocytes) increased significantly two days after primary vaccination (day 2) and were substantially higher two days after secondary vaccination (day 23).

claims.claim_text: Olink assay analysis of plasma from 31 vaccinated individuals showed IFNγ and CXCL10 increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination (day 1 and day 2) and increased even further after secondary immunization (day 21), with plasma IFNγ 11.3-fold higher at day 22 than at day 1.

source.quote: To further investigate this phenomenon, we measured plasma cytokines in 31 vaccinated individuals using Olink ( https://www.olink.com/products/target/inflammation/ ).

Of the 67 cytokines detected, the concentration of 2 cytokines (IFNγ and CXCL10) were increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination ( Fig. 2e left). Similar to our observations on intermediate monocytes and pSTAT1 and pSTAT3, the concentrations of these cytokines were increased even further after the secondary immunization ( Fig. 2e right).
The concentration of plasma IFNγ was 11.3-fold higher at day 22 relative to day 1 ( Fig. 2f ).

comparison.finding: IFNγ and CXCL10 were significantly increased at day 2 compared with day 1 after primary vaccination
